note:
Rebuilt 2026-09-20, three times, and the two failed attempts are the useful part of this note.

THE FIRST PASS fixed the reported sign bug — the name band was at z 0.093 with a canopy at 0.12
reaching out over it and a glazed bay spanning 0.018 to 0.108, so it was behind both. On the
painter a marquee sorts forward of its own wall and drew anyway; on a depth buffer it is simply
not there. That half stands, and `sign:stand` and `signband.mjs` are the two gates for it.

THE SECOND PASS answered "too boxy" by making the tower ROUND — three tapering drums with a
mirrored ring and a dark cap. It stopped being boxy and started being a LIGHTHOUSE. A tapering
cylinder with a lid on it is one of about four things in the world, and none of them sells
clothes; the podium under it read as the shed at the foot of it.

SO THE THIRD PASS PUTS THE SHOPFRONT BACK IN CHARGE, which is what "it does not feel like a
boutique" was actually about. A boutique IS its frontage: the building is a display case you are
allowed to walk into, so the massing has to say that rather than being a tower with a shop under
it. Four moves, none of which is a silhouette gimmick:

  · ONE SLENDER SHAFT, taller than it is wide, instead of a stack of setbacks. Setbacks are what
    an office does because its floor plates shrink; a shop has no reason to and looks like an
    office the moment it pretends to.
  · A FASCIA AT EYE LEVEL, oversailing the glass, carrying the name in script. That band is the
    single most recognisable thing a shop has and the old model did not have one at all.
  · A DEEP CORNICE at the top, oversailing again, with a set-back attic above it. The building
    ends with a brim rather than a lid.
  · A CURVED CORNER ORIEL — one slim full-height drum at the front-right corner. That is the
    round element the second pass wanted, at the size where it reads as a bay window instead of
    as a chimney.

⚠ THE ORIEL IS PEARL AND NOT `ty_aur_frost`, AND THAT IS NOT A COLOUR PREFERENCE. An authored
drum is flat-shaded off WALL_COL — `drawAuthoredModel` builds its skin from the raw RGB and never
reaches `wallTex` — so the milky pane `matFrost` makes of a dark violet key exists only on a BOX.
On a drum the same key is the dark violet it literally is. `ty_aur_pearl` is that answer
pre-mixed, and it is in FROST_WALL all the same because that is what the GL pass shades it by.

⚠ AND EVERY FACE-MOUNTED PART IS ON A BOX. `anchored.mjs` only counts BOX faces as walls, and it
is right to — a flat slab hung off a cylinder stands in air at every point but one — so the oriel
carries no signage, no glazing and no canopy. It is structure, and the boxes either side of it do
the talking.

⚠ THE COLONNADE IS A PILASTER RANK AND THE GLAZING IS NOT. A `windowBay` draws its own bars; a
rank of fins standing proud draws the frame. Both on one face is two sets of mullions a hand
apart, so the shopfront gets the pane and the shaft above it gets the colonnade.

⚠ AND THE ROOF HOARDING IS DECLINED IN `KIT_DECLINE`, by the entry `atelier: [signRoof]`. The
derived kit finds the highest deck on a building and stands a backlit advertising board on legs
on it, which is wrong on this building whoever built it — that is the test for an entry there.

RENDER_TUNE.legacyArms puts the atelier arm back.
